 Cricket-Nicholls hundred rallies New Zealand after Bumrah strikes early for India
 Thursday, 19 Nov 2026
 | 6:13 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 FILE PHOTO: Cricket - International Test Match Series - Fifth Test - England v India - Kia Oval, London, Britain - July 31, 2025 India's Shubman Gill in action Action Images via Reuters/Paul Childs/File Photo 
 Nov 19 (Reuters) - Henry Nicholls scored a brilliant century ⁠to rally New Zealand to 243 for 5 at the close of play after a Jasprit Bumrah-inspired India ⁠had ripped through the top order on the first day of the first test in Wellington on Thursday.
 Paceman ‌Bumrah, who had not played test cricket for a year, dismissed New Zealand captain Tom Latham for a duck with the third delivery of the day to bring Nicholls to the crease as India's bowlers dominated early on at the Basin Reserve.
 Nicholls ground out the runs with great application while the ​wickets continued to fall at the other end, accelerating a little to put ⁠on 39 for the third wicket with Rachin ⁠Ravindra.
 Bumrah (3-52) claimed his third victim in the shape of Tom Blundell shortly after lunch to leave the hosts on the ropes ⁠at ‌70-5 and Glenn Phillips came out to the middle to join Nicholls.
 The pair, finding the batting easier as the day wore on, transformed New Zealand's fortunes in an unbroken partnership of 173 with Nicholls claiming his 12th test century, ⁠a fifth at the Basin Reserve, with a singlelate in the final session.
 All-rounder ​Phillips played an equal part in ‌the partnership, picking up the pace from the start of his innings, and was closing on his second test ⁠century at 94 not ​out at stumps.
 "It was really nice," said Nicholls. "The position we're in (and) to have that partnership with Glenn. 
 "His energy is infectious. The way he came out and put a bit more pressure on them probably allowed me just to go about my work. For us to both be ⁠there at the end of the day is even more pleasing."
 Nicholls will ​resume on day two unbeaten on 113 after a scare on 102 when he spooned a Prasidh Krishna delivery into the air off a top edge.
 Devdutt Padikkal and wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant raced to make the catch but their communication was poor and the square-leg ⁠fielder spilled it into the grass.
 Bumrah apart, India's seam bowling increasingly lacked penetration as the ball got older and questions will be asked in India as to why Anshul Kamboj and Krishna were selected ahead of Mohammed Siraj.
 It was all very different at the start of the day after India skipper Shubman Gill, having looked at the grass on the wicket, won the toss ​and elected to send out the bowlers.
 Bumrah bamboozled Latham with a delivery that moved in ⁠off the seam and rattled the opener's leg stump and Kamboj ensured both New Zealand openers were gone inside the first four ​overs when he had Devon Conway caught behind for four.
 Ravindra scored 15 before ‌swiping at an Akash Deep delivery and edging it behind, and ​Bumrah removed Daryl Mitchell cheaply with the help of a sharp catch from Yashasvi Jaiswal at short leg when he returned for a second spell before lunch.
 (Reporting by Nick Mulvenney, editing by Toby Davis and Edwina Gibbs)
